summary: For a smooth proper f: Y → X over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, the paper proves that tensor invariants of bounded length of π₁(X) on H*(Y_x, F_ℓ) are reductions of those on H*(Y_x, Z_ℓ) for ℓ ≫ 0 (Theorem 1.3). From this it deduces F_ℓ-semisimplicity for ℓ ≫ 0 (Theorem 1.1) and its equivalence with almost hyperspecial image (Theorem 1.2). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed, and five findings are recorded; Theorem 9.1's first two assertions are proved only for ℓ ≥ r (E3). Supplier proofs are deferred. Not formalised.

items.name: Smooth-proper geometric and arithmetic cohomology representations
items.statement: In F construct continuous π and π₀ actions on Hℓ∞,Hℓ,Vℓ∞ and their restriction, base-point transport and finite-field models. Retain the full grading and coefficient topology; total rank is finite and independent of ℓ after the large-prime torsion-free comparison.

api.name: cohomologyRepresentation.restrict_geometric
api.statement: Restriction along the geometric fundamental-group inclusion is the geometric cohomology representation, degree by degree.

api.name: cohomologyRepresentation.coefficient_map
api.statement: The natural integral-to-rational and integral-to-residual cohomology maps are equivariant; the latter is an isomorphism under item22, not without torsion hypotheses.

uses.how: change coefficients and restrict arithmetic action to the geometric group

items.name: Geometric mod-ℓ semisimplicity
items.statement: In F, semisimplicity means every π-stable Fℓ-subspace of Hℓ has a π-stable complement. This concerns the geometric group π, not the arithmetic group π₀.

api.name: geometricSemisimple.iff_retraction
api.statement: Every geometric-stable inclusion admits an equivariant linear retraction if and only if the representation is semisimple.

api.name: geometricSemisimple.directSum
api.statement: A finite direct sum is semisimple if and only if each summand is semisimple.

uses.how: split every stable subspace

items.name: Geometric semisimplicity for all large primes
items.statement: In F there is B(f) such that π acts semisimply on Hℓ for every prime ℓ> B(f), ℓ≠p. Both proof branches §§9 and 10 are extracted separately; no arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity is assumed.

items.name: Hyperspecial and almost-hyperspecial compact subgroup
items.statement: For connected semisimple G/Qℓ, a compact subgroup is hyperspecial if it is 𝒢(Zℓ) for a semisimple Zℓ-model 𝒢 with specified generic-fibre identification. A compact Γ⊂G(Qℓ) is almost hyperspecial when its full inverse image under Gsc(Qℓ)→G(Qℓ) is hyperspecial.

api.name: almostHyperspecial.iff_pullback
api.statement: For semisimple G, the predicate holds exactly when the full inverse image in Gsc(Qℓ) is the Zℓ-points of a semisimple model with its generic-fibre identification.

api.name: almostHyperspecial.conjugate
api.statement: Transporting the model and compact subgroup by a generic-fibre isomorphism preserves hyperspeciality and almost hyperspeciality.

uses.how: pass through the simply connected central cover

items.name: Almost-hyperspecial geometric image
items.statement: In F, after replacing X by one connected finite étale cover independent of ℓ, for all sufficiently large ℓ the geometric image Π∞ is almost hyperspecial in its connected semisimple Qℓ-Zariski closure. This is the equivalence with Theorem 1.1 established in Corollary 8.2, not an assertion that Π∞ itself is hyperspecial.

items.name: Rational Young symmetrizer normalization already built
items.statement: For a tableau t on a Young diagram of size d, the rational group-algebra Young symmetrizer satisfies c_t²=(d!/dim_Q spechtIdeal(t))c_t and (dim_Q spechtIdeal(t)/d!)c_t is idempotent. This is the rational precursor only; no integral coefficient change is credited.

items.name: Integral Young symmetrizers and invertible normalization
items.statement: For λ⊢d construct cλ in Z[S_d], prove cλ²=nλcλ with nλ=d!/dim_Q Sλ a positive divisor of d!, and for a Zℓ-algebra with ℓ>d use nλ⁻¹cλ. Relate the paper's right action/order convention to the existing left-action rational construction explicitly.

api.name: integralYoungProjector.idempotent
api.statement: For λ⊢d and ℓ>d, eλ=nλ⁻¹cλ satisfies eλ²=eλ in the integral group algebra.

api.name: integralYoungProjector.baseChange
api.statement: Under a ring map on which nλ is invertible, the image projector is obtained by applying that map to the integral coefficients.

uses.how: realize Schur functors as coefficient-compatible direct summands

items.name: Integral and mixed Schur functors
items.statement: For finite-free Zℓ-module M with continuous Π-action and λ⊢d with ℓ>d, Sλ(M)=image(nλ⁻¹cλ on M⊗d); put Sλ,μ(M)=Sλ(M)⊗Sμ(M∨), μ⊢e, ℓ>e. Prove functoriality, finite freeness, direct-factor projector, base change, continuity, and symmetric/exterior extreme partitions.

api.name: integralSchur.map_comp
api.statement: Applying the projector to tensor powers of linear maps defines maps preserving identities and composition.

api.name: integralSchur.baseChange
api.statement: The image of the idempotent projector commutes with scalar extension; over Zℓ it is finite free and a direct summand. Mixed functors use the contragredient dual.

uses.how: tensor, dual and reduce lattices

items.name: Invariant reduction predicate
items.statement: InvΠ(M) is the canonical coefficient-reduction isomorphism in convention I. Construct its map, and prove M^Π saturated in M; do not define the predicate as equality of dimensions without constructing the map.

api.name: invariantReduction.map
api.statement: Reduction of fixed vectors induces the canonical injection M^Π/ℓ→(M/ℓ)^Π because the invariant lattice is saturated.

api.name: invariantReduction.iff_H1_no_l_torsion
api.statement: Under the compact-coefficient exact sequence in item10, this injection is surjective exactly when H¹_cont(Π,M)[ℓ]=0.

uses.how: measure the torsion obstruction in H¹

items.name: Invariant reduction and H¹ torsion
items.statement: For a finite free continuous Zℓ-lattice M, surjectivity M^G/ℓ→(M/ℓ)^G is equivalent to H1_cont(G,M)[ℓ]=0 and to Zℓ-torsion-freeness of H1. Item150 supplies the exact sequence directly;151 supplies the DVR torsion argument. For profinite G,148 identifies this with canonical cohomology.

items.name: Invariant reduction for fixed mixed Schur tensors
items.statement: In F, for fixed d,e≥0, uniformly over partitions λ⊢d,μ⊢e, Invπ(Sλ,μ(Hℓ∞)) holds for all sufficiently large ℓ depending on f,d,e.

items.name: Invariant reduction for arithmetic-stable free quotients
items.statement: In F and the same fixed d,e, Invπ(M) holds uniformly for every π₀-equivariant torsion-free quotient Sλ,μ(Hℓ∞)↠M, for all sufficiently large ℓ depending on f,d,e, not the chosen quotient.

items.name: Invariant reduction for arithmetic-stable saturated submodules
items.statement: In F and the same fixed d,e, Invπ(M) holds uniformly for every π₀-stable M⊂Sλ,μ(Hℓ∞) with torsion-free cokernel, for all sufficiently large ℓ depending on f,d,e, not the chosen submodule.

items.name: Symmetric and exterior invariant comparisons
items.statement: Theorem 1.3 specializes to Sym^d, Λ^d and their mixed dual tensors through the row/column partitions. The integral idempotent comparison uses ℓ>d; this is not a claim for arbitrary small characteristic or arbitrary modular Schur subquotients.

items.name: Lisse sheaves and fundamental-group representations
items.statement: For connected X in F and Λ=Zℓ or Fℓ, identify the relevant lisse Λ-sheaves with continuous finite-generated Λ-representations of π₁(X,x), with stalk transport up to the chosen path. Establish H⁰(X,F)=F_x^π and the arithmetic action under descent.

api.name: lisseRepresentation.stalk
api.statement: The chosen geometric stalk gives the continuous fundamental-group representation, with transport under a chosen path.

api.name: lisseRepresentation.globalSections
api.statement: H⁰ of the lisse sheaf identifies with the fixed vectors in that stalk; descent retains the arithmetic quotient action.

uses.how: identify stalk invariants and cohomology

items.name: Arithmetic fundamental-group sequence and fibre Frobenius
items.statement: For the geometrically connected model X₀/k₀, π₁(X,x)→π₁(X₀,x)→Gal(k₀)→1 is exact. A k₀-rational point supplies a section and realizes the Galois action on geometric global sections by its fibre action. Do not add left injectivity without its hypotheses.

items.name: Weil weights with every complex embedding
items.statement: For q>1, a nonzero algebraic number is q-Weil of weight w when all complex embeddings have absolute value q^(w/2). For Frobenius polynomials det(T−F), weights refer to their roots, including multiplicities; duals and Tate twists change weights with geometric-Frobenius conventions.

api.name: weilWeight.mul
api.statement: A product of nonzero algebraic q-Weil numbers of weights a,b has weight a+b, with all complex embeddings tested.

api.name: weilWeight.inv_pow
api.statement: Inversion negates weight; the dth power of a q-Weil number of weight w is q^d-Weil of weight w.

uses.how: separate roots of unequal weights

items.name: Rational compatible family of Frobenius polynomials
items.statement: For sheaves on a finite-field model, require at each closed point away from the coefficient characteristic that det(T−F_x) lies in Q[T] and is independent of ℓ. Compatibility is a property of actual representations, and does not automatically pass to an arbitrary subquotient.

api.name: rationalCompatibleSystem.localPolynomial
api.statement: For each eligible closed point extract the common rational polynomial identified with det(T−F_x) in every realization.

api.name: rationalCompatibleSystem.finiteFieldBaseChange
api.statement: After a residue-field extension of degree d the local roots become their dth powers, preserving coefficient independence.

uses.how: use one Frobenius polynomial for all coefficients

items.name: Primitive integral reduction of rational polynomials
items.statement: For nonzero P=Σa_nT^n∈Q[T], let a(P)>0 have valuations −min_n v_p(a_n) for every prime p. Then a(P)P is primitive integral and its reduction modulo each ℓ is nonzero. Use that reduction when writing P(F)=0 over Fℓ, not an undefined reduction of denominators.

api.name: primitivePolynomial.content_one
api.statement: Multiplication by the unique positive rational a(P) with valuations −min_i v_p(a_i) gives an integral polynomial of content one.

api.name: primitivePolynomial.reduction_ne_zero
api.statement: For nonzero P its primitive integral normalization has nonzero reduction at every prime; degree can drop at primes dividing its leading coefficient.

uses.how: reduce rational annihilators modulo any prime

items.name: Continuous-cohomology object already built
items.statement: For a topological representation A:TopRep k G, continuousCohomology n A is the homology of its complex of invariant homogeneous continuous cochains, as a TopModuleCat k object. This credit does not supply compact-coefficient exactness, ℓ-adic rationalization or the comparison with explicit H¹.

api.name: continuousCohomology.cochain_homology
api.statement: The library object is the homology of the continuous homogeneous-cochain complex in TopRep coefficients.

api.name: continuousCohomology.comparison_request
api.statement: The extension-cocycle application requires a comparison with the explicit H¹ carrier; this is a request, not a credited theorem.

uses.how: reuse the canonical cohomology object

items.name: Gabber–Suh uniform torsion-freeness
items.statement: In F, H*(Yx,Zℓ) is torsion-free for all sufficiently large ℓ, simultaneously in every cohomological degree. Smooth proper base change transports this to the family; the bound concerns a fixed family, not all smooth proper varieties.

items.name: Uniform cohomological reduction
items.statement: In F and for the same large-prime range, the canonical H*(Yx,Zℓ)⊗Fℓ→H*(Yx,Fℓ) is an isomorphism compatible with monodromy. This uses adjacent-degree torsion-freeness, not merely freeness in the displayed degree.

items.name: Smooth-proper rational compatibility and purity
items.statement: For a smooth proper finite-field family, the Frobenius polynomials on R^wf_*Qℓ are rational and independent of ℓ and all roots have weight w. Geometric semisimplicity follows from the pure-lisse theorem on a normal base, not from arithmetic semisimplicity.

items.name: One cover gives connected geometric and arithmetic monodromy
items.statement: In F, after one connected finite étale Galois cover independent of ℓ, all generic geometric Zariski groups are connected semisimple and all arithmetic generic groups are connected. Separate geometric characteristic-zero semisimplicity from independence of the component-group cover.

items.name: Uniform perfect residual geometric image
items.statement: In F, after one connected finite étale Galois cover independent of ℓ, the geometric mod-ℓ images are perfect for every sufficiently large ℓ.

items.name: Uniform order-ℓ generation of residual images
items.statement: With the same kind of fixed cover as Fact 3.4, for every sufficiently large ℓ the residual geometric image is generated by its elements of order ℓ. This is stronger than just having an ℓ-Sylow subgroup and is a separate input to Nori theory.

items.name: Prime-to-index descent for Inv
items.statement: For closed normal open U⊂Π of index prime to ℓ and a finite-free continuous Zℓ-representation M, Inv_U(M) implies Inv_Π(M), by exactness of finite-group invariants after averaging.

items.name: Prime-to-index descent for semisimplicity
items.statement: For U normal open in profinite Π with ℓ∤[Π:U], a finite-dimensional continuous Fℓ-representation semisimple upon restriction to U is semisimple for Π. Average a U-equivariant splitting over Π/U; normality and invertibility of the index are essential.

items.name: Geometric monodromy comparison with a finite-field curve
items.statement: In F there exist a smooth geometrically connected finite-field curve, a smooth proper family over it and one fixed normal open subgroup U of the original π such that their geometric images identify on Zℓ and Fℓ cohomology for all sufficiently large ℓ. The construction uses Bertini, spreading, tame specialization and smooth proper base change; an arbitrary arithmetic specialization does not give this assertion.

items.name: Bertini curve with fundamental-group surjection
items.statement: After permissible finitely generated-field/base-point enlargement, choose a smooth geometrically connected curve mapping to X₀ whose geometric π₁ surjects onto the required geometric monodromy quotient; preserve the restricted smooth proper family. This is the source-qualified Jouanolou input to Lemma 4.3, not a claim that every curve has surjective π₁.

api.name: bertiniMonodromyCurve.map
api.statement: Expose the smooth connected curve and its morphism into the original base under the Bertini hypotheses.

api.name: bertiniMonodromyCurve.pi1_surjective
api.statement: The supplied fundamental-group map is surjective, so restricting any representation preserves its image.

uses.how: reduce the geometric image to dimension one

items.name: Uniform tame reduction and specialization
items.statement: Use de Jong to make boundary inertia potentially unipotent uniformly in ℓ on one cover; for ℓ≠p unipotent congruence images are pro-ℓ, so wild pro-p inertia is killed. Specialize the resulting tame representation to a finite-field curve and compare fibres by smooth proper base change. Retain the one-cover quantifier and both coefficient levels.

items.name: Alteration with smooth compactification and normal-crossing boundary
items.statement: For the integral finite-type schemes over the perfect fields arising in §§4–5, use a proper dominant generically finite, generically étale alteration to a smooth scheme admitting a smooth projective compactification with strict normal-crossing boundary. Restrict to an open on which it is finite étale of degree δ before using trace splitting.

items.name: Fibre-power Künneth realization of total tensor powers
items.statement: For the d-fold fibre product of the smooth proper family, integral Künneth gives H*(Yx^[d],Zℓ)≅H*(Yx,Zℓ)⊗d after all torsion terms vanish; the comparison is arithmetic-equivariant and compatible with reduction. Rational or derived Künneth alone is not the integral direct-sum statement.

items.name: Poincaré duality with twist and support retained
items.statement: For smooth pure-dimensional Y over an algebraically closed field, coefficients Λ=Qℓ or Fℓ, ℓ≠p, there is Frobenius-equivariant perfect duality H^i(Y,Λ)≅H_c^(2dimY−i)(Y,Λ)(dimY)∨. For proper smooth fibres this identifies dual cohomology with complementary degree and the correct Tate twist; integral use requires its torsion-free comparison.

items.name: Schur direct-factor inheritance of invariant reduction
items.statement: For 0≤d,e<ℓ, the normalized Young projectors make Sλ,μ(M) a Π-equivariant direct summand of M⊗d⊗(M∨)⊗e. Inv for the ambient tensor object implies Inv for that summand; extend the reduction to arithmetic-stable free quotients and saturated submodules with the induced projector maps.

items.name: Reduction to untensored finite-field curve results
items.statement: Theorem 4.5 for ordinary cohomology on finite-field curves implies Theorem 1.3 in F, by Lemmas 4.2–4.4, fibre powers, finite direct sums, duality and twists. The same curve reduction transfers the geometric semisimplicity assertion. The integral Frobenius-projector dévissage is supplied in item 116.

items.name: Curve invariant reduction
items.statement: In C, for all sufficiently large ℓ, Invπ(H*(Yx,Zℓ)) holds.

items.name: Curve free-quotient invariant reduction
items.statement: In C and for all sufficiently large ℓ uniformly over the quotient, Invπ(M) holds for every π₀-equivariant torsion-free quotient of H*(Yx,Zℓ). The proof first treats a single degree and uses an affine restriction.

items.name: Curve saturated-submodule invariant reduction
items.statement: In C and for all sufficiently large ℓ uniformly over the submodule, Invπ(M) holds for every π₀-stable saturated submodule of H*(Yx,Zℓ). The determinant and exterior-dual proof must retain arithmetic twists while using geometric determinant triviality.

items.name: Torsion characteristic polynomial divides reduction
items.statement: For a finitely generated Zℓ-module H and a Zℓ-linear automorphism F, charpoly(F|H[ℓ]) divides charpoly(F|H/ℓH). For finite H the two Fℓ[F]-modules have equal classes in the finite-length Grothendieck group and hence equal semisimplifications, not necessarily an isomorphism.

items.name: Characteristic polynomial commutes with base change
items.statement: For R commutative, M finite free over R, f∈End_R(M) and commutative R-algebra A, charpoly(f_A)=map(R→A,charpoly(f)). This general theorem covers rationalization and reduction of a free lattice; it does not by itself prove Lemma 5.1 for torsion H.

items.name: Uniform compact-support annihilator over Qℓ
items.statement: For separated finite-type Y₀/F_q and w≥0, there is nonzero P≤w,Y₀∈Q[T] independent of ℓ≠p, all roots q-Weil of weights≤w, annihilating geometric Frobenius on H_c^w(Y,Qℓ) for every ℓ≠p. This is an annihilator, not a claimed ℓ-independent characteristic polynomial of arbitrary nonproper cohomology.

items.name: Uniform compact-support annihilator modulo ℓ
items.statement: For the same Y₀,w, the primitive-integral reduction of a common P≤w,Y₀ as in 42 annihilates H_c^w(Y,Fℓ) for every sufficiently large ℓ. No Weil weight is directly assigned to an Fℓ eigenvalue; it is controlled by reduction of a rational polynomial.

items.name: Annihilator descent and dimension induction
items.statement: Descend a bound from F_q^d using P(T^d). Reduce nilpotents, separate irreducible components by lower-dimensional closed strata, alter the open integral part, and use localization to multiply annihilators. Choose one alteration first, then exclude primes dividing its degree; retain the compact-support groups throughout.

api.name: uniformAnnihilator.constantExtension
api.statement: An annihilator P for F^d pulls back to P(T^d) for F.

api.name: uniformAnnihilator.localization_product
api.statement: For the compact-support localization sequence, multiply annihilators on the open and closed pieces; use trace descent only away from the fixed alteration degree.

uses.how: perform dimension induction with compact support

items.name: Finite étale compact-support trace splitting
items.statement: For finite étale U′→U of degree δ over a finite field and Λ=Qℓ or Fℓ with δ invertible, pullback and trace on H_c^w compose to δ·id. Thus H_c^w(U,Λ) is a Frobenius-equivariant direct summand of H_c^w(U′,Λ), not ordinary H^w(U′,Λ).

items.name: Curve Leray edge and high-weight annihilator
items.statement: In C, for Λ=Qℓ (all ℓ≠p) or Fℓ (all sufficiently large ℓ), H¹(X,R^wf_*Λ)=E₂^(1,w)=E∞^(1,w) is a subquotient of H^(w+1)(Y,Λ). Smooth duality and 42–43 produce a common rational annihilator P≥w+1 with roots of weights≥w+1; for dimY=D use T^degP P(q^D/T) from P≤2D−w−1.

items.name: Weight-separated annihilators kill torsion
items.statement: In C the ℓ-torsion of H¹(X,R^wf_*Zℓ) is killed by reduction of P_w from a rational-point fibre (roots weight w) and by P≥w+1. Distinct weights make the rational polynomials coprime; a nonzero integer Bézout resultant excludes finitely many primes, making the two reduced polynomials coprime and forcing the torsion module to vanish.

items.name: Affine curve H¹ quotient surjectivity
items.statement: For X a smooth affine geometric curve and finite-free continuous Zℓ representations H↠M with free kernel, the requisite cdℓ≤1 and compact-coefficient comparison give H¹(π,H)↠H¹(π,M). In the arithmetic-equivariant single-degree application H=H^w(Yx,Zℓ), this transports the same high-weight annihilator to every quotient M.

items.name: Geometric determinants of saturated submodules are trivial
items.statement: After the fixed covers of Facts 3.3–4, Π∞ has finite abelianization and is generated by pro-ℓ Sylows. For large ℓ>2, its determinant character on any invariant free submodule M has finite image in Zℓ× of order dividing ℓ−1, so is trivial. This conclusion is geometric; the arithmetic determinant character may be nontrivial.

items.name: Determinant duality reduces saturated submodules to quotients
items.statement: For M free of rank m≥1, the wedge map identifies M with (Λ^(m−1)M)∨⊗det(M). For M saturated in a single H^w, dualizing and exterior powers give an arithmetic-equivariant free quotient of a complementary-degree fibre-power cohomology group, with Tate twist. Apply quotient Inv after accounting for the geometrically trivial determinant. Treat m=0 separately.

api.name: determinantDuality.equiv
api.statement: For m>0, wedge evaluation identifies M with (Λ^(m−1)M)∨⊗det(M), equivariantly for the full arithmetic action.

api.name: determinantDuality.geometricUntwist
api.statement: If the geometric determinant is trivial the geometric representation untwists, while the arithmetic determinant character must still be retained.

uses.how: treat saturated rank-m submodules by free quotients

items.name: Integral monodromy closure and its two fibres
items.statement: For a compact image Π∞⊂GL(H) with H finite free over Zℓ, form the reduced schematic Zariski closure 𝒢 in GL(H), generic group Gη⊂GL(H⊗Qℓ), special group Gs⊂GL(H⊗Fℓ). It is flat over Zℓ and dimGs=dimGη; smoothness and connectedness of Gs are conclusions later, not part of this definition.

api.name: integralMonodromy.genericFiber
api.statement: The schematic closure in GL(H) has generic fibre the rational Zariski closure of the image.

api.name: integralMonodromy.flat
api.statement: Its defining ideal is the contraction of the generic ideal, so the coordinate ring is torsion free over the DVR and flat; smoothness is a later theorem.

uses.how: compare generic and special fibres

items.name: Subgroup generated by ℓ-Sylows
items.statement: For closed Π⊂GL_r(Zℓ) or GL_r(Fℓ), Π+ is the closed normal subgroup generated by its ℓ-Sylow subgroups. In the finite residual, dimension-bounded large-prime setting it is generated by order-ℓ elements. Distinguish abstract generation, closed generation, reduction image and full algebraic envelope.

api.name: plusSubgroup.minimal
api.statement: The closed subgroup generated by all pro-ℓ Sylow subgroups is contained in every closed subgroup containing those Sylows.

api.name: plusSubgroup.characteristic
api.statement: Automorphisms preserve the collection of Sylows, so the closed generated subgroup is characteristic and normal.

uses.how: compare residual and compact plus groups

items.name: Bounded mixed tensor space
items.statement: For finite free H set T≤d(H)=⊕_{0≤s,t≤d}H⊗s⊗(H∨)⊗t. The bounds are separate, so total tensor length can be 2d. Define the pointwise group-scheme stabilizer of its invariant submodule, not merely its setwise stabilizer.

api.name: boundedMixedTensor.summand
api.statement: For s≤d and t≤d, include M^⊗s⊗(M∨)^⊗t as its specified direct summand.

api.name: boundedMixedTensor.action_degree
api.statement: For an exponential root subgroup on rank-r M each summand action has parameter degree at most (s+t)(r−1), hence at most 2d(r−1).

uses.how: bound polynomial degree and stabilize tensors

items.name: Truncated exponential and logarithm for order-ℓ matrices
items.statement: For ℓ≥r and g∈GL_r(Fℓ) of order ℓ, log(g)=−Σ_{1≤i<ℓ}(1−g)^i/i and exp(tlogg)=Σ_{0≤i<ℓ}(tlogg)^i/i! define a unipotent one-parameter subgroup φ_g:G_a→GL_r. Prove the polynomial inverse identities under the nilpotence/large-prime bound.

api.name: truncatedExpLog.inverse
api.statement: In characteristic ℓ≥r, the degree<r exponential and logarithm are inverse on matrices with N^r=0 and (g−1)^r=0.

api.name: truncatedExpLog.oneParameter
api.statement: For fixed N^r=0, exp((a+b)N)=exp(aN)exp(bN), and exp(0N)=1, as polynomial identities.

uses.how: pass between nilpotent matrices and unipotents

items.name: Nori exponential envelope
items.statement: For Π⊂GL_r(Fℓ), N(Π) is the algebraic subgroup generated by the one-parameter groups φ_g for its order-ℓ elements. It is smooth connected and generated by unipotents; define generation scheme-theoretically and prove independence of choices. This symbol is separate from the composition-factor product used in §8.

api.name: noriEnvelope.minimal
api.statement: The envelope is the smallest closed algebraic subgroup containing every one-parameter exponential attached to an order-ℓ element.

api.name: noriEnvelope.conjugate
api.statement: Conjugating the residual representation conjugates each exponential subgroup and its generated envelope.

uses.how: replace the finite image by an algebraic group

items.name: Nori finite-points plus comparison
items.statement: For ℓ sufficiently large depending only on r, N(Π)(Fℓ)+=Π+. This is the group-theoretic input from Nori, not a consequence of Zariski density of the finite set Π.

items.name: Nori invariant-subspace comparison
items.statement: Under the same bound, Π+ and N(Π) have exactly the same invariant Fℓ-subspaces of H=Fℓ^r. Scheme-representation invariance is compared with the finite-group action; this does not assert every rational representation is semisimple.

items.name: Uniform bounded-tensor stabilizer
items.statement: There is d(r), independent of ℓ and Π in the large-prime range, such that N(Π) equals the pointwise group-scheme stabilizer in GL(H) of T≤d(r)(H)^N(Π). Its uniformity and scheme-level strength are indispensable. This is the Cadoret–Tamagawa 2016 tensor-stabilizer input, distinct from Nori Theorem B.

items.name: Bounded tensor invariants agree
items.statement: For each fixed d and ℓ sufficiently large depending on r,d, T≤d(H)^N(Π)=T≤d(H)^Π+. For the polynomial interpolation step ℓ>2d(r−1) suffices once the exponential construction is valid; do not replace this with ℓ>d alone.

items.name: Simply connected integral points are plus-generated
items.statement: If 𝒮/Zℓ is a simply connected semisimple group scheme, then 𝒮(Zℓ)=𝒮(Zℓ)+. Use surjectivity of smooth reduction with pro-ℓ kernel and generation of 𝒮(Fℓ) by ℓ-elements.

items.name: Special monodromy fibre equals Nori envelope
items.statement: In G, for every sufficiently large ℓ, Gs=Nℓ as closed group schemes in GL(Hℓ). Invariant reduction and 58–59 give Gs⊂Nℓ; Larsen's dimension comparison and flat dimension equality force equality. Equality of Fℓ-points alone is insufficient.

items.name: Special-fibre plus image is perfect and enveloping
items.statement: In G and for all large ℓ, Gs(Fℓ)+ is perfect and Gs is the Nori envelope of Gs(Fℓ). Preserve both assertions as consequences of 61 and Nori's plus comparison.

items.name: Uniform weak maximality index bound
items.statement: In G, there is C_r depending only on r=rank Hℓ∞ with [𝒢(Zℓ):Π∞]≤C_r for all sufficiently large ℓ. This uses Larsen 2010 Theorem 7; bounded index is not index one.

items.name: Geometric image equals integral-points plus subgroup
items.statement: In G and for all sufficiently large ℓ, Π∞=𝒢(Zℓ)+. Combine plus-generation of Π∞, the pro-ℓ congruence kernel and the bounded-index theorem after ℓ>C_r.

items.name: Integral geometric monodromy closure is smooth connected
items.statement: In G and for all sufficiently large ℓ, 𝒢 is a smooth connected Zℓ-group scheme: flatness and smoothness of generic and Nori special fibres yield smoothness. Semisimplicity of the special fibre is not yet proved.

items.name: Residual and algebraic module semisimplicity agree
items.statement: In G and for all large ℓ, Hℓ is semisimple under Πℓ iff it is semisimple as a representation of Nℓ=Gs, by equality of invariant subspaces.

items.name: Faithful semisimple Nori module forces semisimple group
items.statement: In G, semisimplicity of the faithful Gs-module Hℓ implies Gs reductive. Its generation by unipotents removes the central torus, hence Gs is semisimple. Faithful semisimple representation alone would only give reductivity.

items.name: Low-dimensional representations in large characteristic
items.statement: For a connected semisimple algebraic group over Fℓ, its r-dimensional rational representation is semisimple when ℓ is sufficiently large in terms of r, in the Jantzen/Larsen range used here. The exact cited bound remains external-input gap G1; no Maschke argument with ℓ dividing the group order is allowed.

items.name: Fibre semisimplicity and integral semisimple model
items.statement: For the smooth connected 𝒢 of 65 with semisimple generic fibre, Gs semisimple iff 𝒢 is a semisimple Zℓ-group scheme. This is the final equivalence (3)↔(4) of Corollary 7.5, not a definition of an arbitrary flat model as smooth.

items.name: Field-level semisimple and reductive groups already built
items.statement: For finite-type commutative Hopf algebras over a field k, semisimplicity means smoothness and geometric connectedness with no nontrivial smooth connected normal solvable geometric closed subgroup. The pinned scheme-side reductive predicate transports the analogous unipotent-radical condition through the affine Hopf anti-equivalence. These field-level predicates do not supply relative semisimplicity over Zℓ.

api.name: fieldSemisimple.geometricCriterion
api.statement: The pinned predicate requires smoothness and geometric connectedness and excludes every nontrivial smooth connected normal solvable geometric subgroup.

api.name: fieldSemisimple.affineHopf
api.statement: Transport the field-level group predicate through the existing affine group / Hopf algebra anti-equivalence.

uses.how: distinguish field predicates from integral models

items.name: Field-level semisimple implies reductive already built
items.statement: Every semisimple finite-type commutative Hopf algebra over a field is reductive, since each smooth connected normal unipotent geometric closed subgroup is solvable. This is a structural implication only, not complete reducibility of all positive-characteristic representations.

items.name: Hyperspecial points and semisimple integral models
items.statement: For connected semisimple G/Qℓ use the building of Gsc with Gad(Qℓ)-action. Semisimple Zℓ-models with their generic identifications correspond to hyperspecial points; an isogeny extends uniquely between the models attached to the same point. Import buildings and parahoric models, and prove this precise hyperspecial correspondence.

api.name: hyperspecialModel.genericIdentification
api.statement: Expose the semisimple model and its specified identification with the given generic group at the hyperspecial point.

api.name: hyperspecialModel.isogenyExtension
api.statement: A central isogeny of generic groups extends between the models attached to the same building point under the Bruhat–Tits hypotheses.

uses.how: compare simply connected integral models

items.name: Hyperspecial maximal compactness
items.statement: A hyperspecial subgroup of a connected semisimple Qℓ-group is maximal among compact subgroups and has maximal volume; its conjugates are hyperspecial. Retain the specified Haar-volume comparison when used, rather than claiming every maximal compact is hyperspecial.

items.name: Nonabelian composition-factor product
items.statement: For a profinite group Π with an open normal pro-ℓ subgroup, define cna(Π) as the product, with multiplicity, of orders of nonabelian simple factors of a finite quotient by such a subgroup. Prove independence of the quotient using that finite ℓ-groups have only abelian composition factors. Do not multiply an infinite composition series.

api.name: nonabelianFactorProduct.independent_quotient
api.statement: Quotienting by different open normal pro-ℓ subgroups gives the same product of orders of nonabelian simple factors, since finite ℓ-groups have only abelian factors.

api.name: nonabelianFactorProduct.abelian_extension
api.statement: An extension with abelian kernel preserves this product; for finite groups the product is multiplicative across a normal subgroup and its quotient.

uses.how: compare compact groups by finite quotients

items.name: Composition-factor product under subgroups and abelian extensions
items.statement: For the finite-by-pro-ℓ groups in 74, a closed subgroup Π′⊂Π satisfies cna(Π′)≤cna(Π). Extensions with abelian kernel or abelian quotient leave cna unchanged. Establish the finite-group reduction and composition-factor argument, not an unsupported equality of orders.

items.name: Smooth integral reduction with pro-ℓ kernel
items.statement: For smooth connected affine finite-type 𝓗/Zℓ, 𝓗(Zℓ)→𝓗(Fℓ) is surjective with pro-ℓ kernel. It preserves cna, also after taking plus subgroups. This is the Hensel/congruence result required by Lemma 8.1.

items.name: Solvable-radical quotient preserves nonabelian factors
items.statement: For smooth connected affine H/Fℓ, Lang's theorem makes H(Fℓ)→(H/R(H))(Fℓ) surjective. For sufficiently large ℓ relative to rank, passing to this semisimple quotient or to plus subgroups preserves cna; central-isogeny cokernels have bounded order and are abelian.

items.name: Uniform finite Lie-type composition-factor bounds
items.statement: For connected semisimple H/Fℓ of dimension d and bounded rank, for all sufficiently large ℓ its nonabelian factors are those of almost-simple factors H_i(Fℓ)+ modulo their centres. There is a rank-dependent c>0 with (ℓ−1)^d/c≤cna(H(Fℓ))≤(ℓ+1)^d. Keep the small-field exceptions and central-isogeny indices explicit.

items.name: Semisimple model comparison via simply connected cover
items.statement: Let G/Qℓ be connected semisimple and 𝒢,𝒮 smooth connected integral models of G,Gsc. Assume 𝒮 semisimple and (psc)⁻¹(𝒢(Zℓ)+) normal in 𝒮(Zℓ) with abelian quotient. For ℓ sufficiently large depending only on dimG, 𝒢 is semisimple. The proof compares cna bounds to force dim(Gs/R(Gs))=dimG; the use of affineness of models is a carrier verification in G4.

items.name: Simply connected pullback of integral-points plus subgroup
items.statement: For semisimple 𝒢/Zℓ and its simply connected semisimple model 𝒮 at the same hyperspecial point, for all large ℓ, (psc)⁻¹(𝒢(Zℓ)+)=𝒮(Zℓ), and 𝒮(Zℓ)↠𝒢(Zℓ)+. Prove the first equality by finite-kernel compactness and maximal compactness; the second uses bounded exponent of the generic central-isogeny cokernel and plus-generation.

items.name: Semisimplicity iff almost hyperspecial
items.statement: In G and for all sufficiently large ℓ, the four conditions of Corollary 7.5 are equivalent to Π∞ almost hyperspecial in Gη(Qℓ). Forward: 64 and 80. Reverse: Lemma 8.1 applied to the hyperspecial preimage and the smooth model 65.

items.name: Invariant-dimension defect
items.statement: In L, for finite-free algebraic 𝒢-representation M, Δ_H(M)=dim_Fℓ((M⊗Fℓ)^(Gs)°)−dim_Qℓ((M⊗Qℓ)^Gη). Construct the generic invariant lattice and reduction injection to prove nonnegativity. The special identity component, not the whole special group, is part of the definition.

api.name: invariantDefect.nonnegative
api.statement: The saturated generic invariant lattice reduces injectively into the special identity-component invariants, so Δ≥0.

api.name: invariantDefect.directSum
api.statement: The defect of a finite direct sum is the sum of the defects, with the same special identity-component convention.

uses.how: detect special-fibre radical by dual Lie exterior powers

items.name: Nice integral model of a maximal torus
items.statement: The nice-model predicate is convention L's extension of a CLOSED split-torus embedding after finite splitting E/Qℓ, with integral lattice H⊗O_E. Prove it invariant under permitted basis change and faithful flat scalar extension; extending only the pointwise torus action is weaker.

api.name: niceTorus.closedEmbedding
api.statement: Expose the finite splitting field E and closed immersion of the split torus over O_E extending the given generic embedding.

api.name: niceTorus.basisChange
api.statement: Conjugation by an integral lattice automorphism transports the torus extension and preserves its closed-immersion property.

uses.how: apply the nice-model criterion to compatible Frobenius

items.name: Nice torus implies smooth integral closure in large characteristic
items.statement: In L with a nice torus and sufficiently large ℓ (in particular ℓ≥r for the displayed root-exponential proof), 𝒢 is smooth over Zℓ. The printed 9.1.1 omits this bound; record E3 and do not export an unrestricted small-prime theorem from this proof.

items.name: Nice torus preserves reductive rank and root inclusion
items.statement: Under 84's hypotheses, (Gs)°/Ru((Gs)°) has rank s equal to rankGη, and its geometric root system is a subsystem of that of Gη. Use the special torus and Lie-weight comparison; preserve residue-field/base-extension distinctions.

items.name: Exterior Lie-defect criterion for semisimple models
items.statement: In L with a nice torus, for ℓ sufficiently large depending only on r, write 𝔤=Lie𝒢⊂H⊗H∨. Then 𝒢 is semisimple iff Δ_H(Λ^n𝔤∨)≤0 for every 1≤n≤δ. The bound is on representation dimension, and exterior powers are of the DUAL integral Lie lattice.

items.name: Integral root groups and big-cell smoothness
items.statement: After faithfully flat base change to O_E splitting the nice torus, take primitive generators Nα of root-line intersections with End(H). For ℓ≥r, t↦exp(tNα) identifies their closures with G_a; the ordered U+×T×U− multiplication gives the open big cell. Descend smoothness and the root/rank statement. Do not identify a ramified O_E with Zℓ as rings.

api.name: integralBigCell.rootMap
api.statement: For a primitive root-line generator Nα and ℓ≥r, expose the integral polynomial map t↦exp(tNα).

api.name: integralBigCell.multiplication
api.statement: The ordered root groups and split torus have an open-immersion multiplication map under the cited Bruhat–Tits hypotheses; descend smoothness by faithful flatness.

uses.how: prove smoothness after a possibly ramified splitting extension

items.name: First exterior defect excludes the reductive centre
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 86 and Δ_H(𝔤∨)≤0, the reductive quotient of (Gs)° is semisimple. The exact Lie sequence and its dual inject (𝔤rd)∨ into 𝔤s∨; large-characteristic semisimplicity/self-duality of the adjoint module and the zero generic adjoint invariants bound its centre dimension by zero.

items.name: Exterior-adjoint invariant Poincaré polynomial
items.statement: For connected semisimple groups of rank s in characteristic zero, and in sufficiently large positive characteristic depending on s, the dimensions of (Λ^m𝔤)^G are the coefficients of P_G(T)=∏_j(1+T^(2e_j+1)), the multiset e_j of Weyl exponents over all almost-simple factors. For a product, use Λ*(V⊕W)≅Λ*V⊗Λ*W. Prove the large-characteristic transfer, not just the complex Lie-group formula.

items.name: Equal rank and smaller dimension force an exterior invariant excess
items.statement: For connected semisimple G/Fℓ and G′/Qℓ of the same rank s, ℓ sufficiently large depending on s, if dimG<dimG′ then some 0≤m≤dimG has dim(Λ^mLieG)^G>dim(Λ^mLieG′)^G′. The Poincaré polynomials have the same value 2^s at 1 and different degree, forcing a coefficient excess below dimG.

items.name: All exterior defects remove the unipotent radical
items.statement: With 85,88–90 and all Δ_H(Λ^n𝔤∨)≤0, the reductive quotient has dimension δ, so the unipotent radical vanishes. The integral connectedness theorem gives connected special fibre, hence a semisimple model. Conversely semisimple group schemes have locally constant root datum/Poincaré polynomial, giving defect zero.

items.name: Γ-regular semisimple element
items.statement: For reductive G⊂GL(V) in characteristic zero, a regular semisimple g in its unique maximal torus Tg is Γ-regular when every automorphism of Tg over the algebraic closure fixing g and preserving the formal character is trivial, and the only GL(V)-conjugate of Tg containing g is Tg itself.

api.name: gammaRegular.uniqueTorus
api.statement: The regular element lies in a unique maximal torus and satisfies the additional formal-character-preserving automorphism and conjugate-torus conditions.

api.name: gammaRegular.conjugate
api.statement: Conjugating the embedded group and element transports these conditions and the resulting torus.

uses.how: identify and split the Frobenius torus

items.name: Compatible Frobenius gives a nice torus
items.statement: In G, apply Larsen–Pink to the arithmetic semisimplification and lift its Γ-regular torus across the unipotent radical of G′η. One suitable closed point x₀ with common rational polynomial P_x₀, and exclusion of the discriminant primes of its squarefree part, gives integral eigenspace decompositions and a nice model of a geometric maximal torus for all sufficiently large ℓ. Uniformity in the chosen point and the torus lift are external-input checks, not consequences of rational compatibility alone.

items.name: Arithmetic-stable Lie lattice and tensor quotients
items.statement: In G, normality Π∞⊲Π′∞ makes the saturated lattice 𝔤=Lie𝒢⊂End(Hℓ∞) arithmetic-stable. Smoothness identifies its special reduction with LieGs. Dualizing the saturated inclusion and taking exterior powers supplies π₀-equivariant free quotients H⊗n⊗(H∨)⊗n↠Λ^n𝔤∨, with n≤δ≤r².

api.name: arithmeticLieLattice.normality_stable
api.statement: Normality of geometric monodromy in arithmetic monodromy makes the saturated Lie lattice arithmetic-stable.

api.name: arithmeticLieLattice.exteriorDualQuotient
api.statement: Dualizing the saturated Lie inclusion in End(H) and taking exterior powers gives the arithmetic-equivariant free tensor quotients onto Λ^n Lie∨.

uses.how: apply Theorem1.3 to free quotients

items.name: Tensor invariant reduction forces Lie defects zero
items.statement: Apply Theorem 1.3(1) to 94. Since Gs is connected by Theorem 7.3, dim M^Gs≤dim M^Πℓ in characteristic ℓ, while generic algebraic and Π∞ invariants agree by Zariski density. Integral invariant reduction gives Δ_H(M)≤0 for every Λ^n𝔤∨; then 86 and Corollary 7.5 prove Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Splitting invariant exterior vectors splits a determinant line
items.statement: In G, let A⊂Hℓ be a Πℓ-submodule of dimension a≥1. If (Λ^aHℓ)^Πℓ↪Λ^aHℓ splits equivariantly, then Λ^aA↪Λ^aHℓ splits: Πℓ+ generation kills the determinant character to Fℓ×, so Λ^aA is a trivial line within the invariant subspace.

items.name: A split determinant inclusion splits the submodule
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional representation H over a field and a stable a-dimensional subspace A, a≥1, an equivariant retraction s:Λ^aH→Λ^aA induces H→A by v↦[u↦s(v∧Λ^(a−1)ι(u))] and A≅Hom(Λ^(a−1)A,Λ^aA). It retracts A↪H, with no division by a. The zero-dimensional subspace splits separately.

items.name: Exterior powers and induced linear maps already built
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and R-modules M,N, the exterior power has its alternating universal property/presentation; f:M→ₗ[R]N induces exteriorPower.map n f:Λ^nM→ₗ[R]Λ^nN. This credits the module construction only, not the determinant splitting or integral representation comparison.

api.name: exteriorPower.map_generators
api.statement: The exterior map sends v₁∧…∧v_n to f(v₁)∧…∧f(v_n).

api.name: exteriorPower.ext
api.statement: Linear maps from an exterior power agreeing on all pure wedges agree everywhere.

uses.how: use the existing alternating carrier

items.name: Invariant splitting suffices for geometric semisimplicity
items.statement: By 96–97, it suffices to split invariant inclusions in every exterior power of each H^w(Yx,Fℓ). For ℓ>a the exterior power is a direct factor of H^(wa)(Yx^[a],Fℓ); apply the same invariant-splitting assertion to this smooth proper fibre power. Uniformity over a is finite since a≤rank H^w.

items.name: Canonical invariant lattice and quotient reduce exactly
items.statement: Set A∞=Hℓ∞^Π∞ and B∞=Hℓ∞/A∞; A∞ is saturated and B∞ free. Fact 3.1 and Inv identify A∞/ℓ=Aℓ=Hℓ^Πℓ and B∞/ℓ=Bℓ=Hℓ/Aℓ, giving 0→B∞ --ℓ→B∞→Bℓ→0. Keep the canonical reduction diagram and snake connecting map; a dimension count alone does not construct it.

api.name: invariantLatticeSequence.quotientFree
api.statement: The invariant lattice is saturated, so its quotient in a finite-free Zℓ-lattice is finite free.

api.name: invariantLatticeSequence.reductionExact
api.statement: Under Inv and cohomological reduction, reducing the canonical short exact lattice sequence gives exactly the fixed-space inclusion and quotient over Fℓ.

uses.how: construct the mod-ℓ extension to split

items.name: Continuous H¹ class of a representation extension
items.statement: For an exact sequence0→A→H→B→0 of finite free continuous G-lattices over a complete DVR R, choose the continuous R-linear section149. The cocycle c_s(g)=g*s*g⁻¹−s, valued in Hom_R(B,A), defines an independent class in the existing explicit H1. It vanishes exactly when an equivariant continuous section exists, and its reduction and fraction-field images are the corresponding extension classes. For profinite G,148 transports it to canonical cohomology.

api.name: continuousExtensionClass.cocycle
api.statement: The section s defines c_s(g)=g*s*g⁻¹−s in Hom(B,A), a continuous cocycle.

api.name: continuousExtensionClass.change_section
api.statement: Replacing s by s+i*a adds the boundary of a.

api.name: continuousExtensionClass.zero_iff_split
api.statement: The class vanishes precisely when the extension has a continuous equivariant R-linear section.

api.name: continuousExtensionClass.baseChange
api.statement: Reduction modulo π and extension to K carry the class to the class of the changed extension under the finite free Hom comparison.

uses.how: Descend rational splitting through the injective H1 coefficient map151.

items.name: Saturated arithmetic Hom lattice has torsion-free H¹
items.statement: In 100, the module A∞⊗B∞∨ embeds as an arithmetic-stable saturated submodule of Hℓ∞⊗Hℓ∞∨. Theorem 1.3(2) and 10 give H¹(Π∞,A∞⊗B∞∨)[ℓ]=0. Arithmetic normality is essential to justify use of Theorem 1.3.

items.name: Cohomological proof of geometric semisimplicity
items.statement: The extension class101 becomes zero over Qℓ by connected semisimple generic monodromy. By102 its integral H1 group has no ℓ-torsion, and the direct kernel lemma151 makes H1(M)→H1(M⊗Qℓ) injective. Hence the integral extension splits, so does its reduction, and the exterior/determinant reduction99 gives Theorem1.1. Full compact localization152 is available but is not needed for this implication.

items.name: Arithmetic semisimplicity and Tate fullness assertions
items.statement: For K₀ finitely generated over F_p, smooth proper d-dimensional Y₀/K₀, Y=Y₀×K̄₀ and w≥0, (11.1,Λ,w) asks semisimplicity of Gal(K₀) on H^(2w)(Y,Λ); (11.2,Λ,w) asks surjectivity of Z^w(Y₀)⊗Λ→H^(2w)(Y,Λ(w))^Gal(K₀). Keep Λ=Zℓ,Fℓ,Qℓ separate and do not assert these conjectures.

api.name: arithmeticTateAssertions.cycleMap
api.statement: Expose the cycle-class map in codimension w into arithmetic fixed vectors of H^(2w)(Y,Λ(w)).

api.name: arithmeticTateAssertions.fullness
api.statement: Tate fullness is surjectivity of that map for the specified coefficient ring; it is distinct from semisimplicity of the arithmetic representation.

uses.how: retain all conditional hypotheses

items.name: Conditional arithmetic mod-ℓ semisimplicity
items.statement: For 104, assuming (11.1,Qℓ,w) and (11.2,Qℓ,i) for i=w,d−w in the source's rational-coefficient hypothesis, conclude (11.1,Fℓ,w) for all sufficiently large ℓ depending on Y₀. This is conditional and in positive characteristic; it is not an unconditional arithmetic variant of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Conditional arithmetic mod-ℓ Tate fullness
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as 105, conclude (11.2,Fℓ,w) for all sufficiently large ℓ. Complementary-codimension Tate fullness d−w is needed for the integral cycle-saturation input and cannot be dropped.

items.name: Integral cycle saturation from rational Tate hypotheses
items.statement: In 104 under the rational assumptions of Corollary 11.1, for all sufficiently large ℓ the cycle map Z^w(Y₀)⊗Zℓ→H^(2w)(Y,Zℓ(w))^Gal(K₀) is surjective and its map to all integral cohomology has torsion-free cokernel. This is the precise Milne–Ramachandran Lemma 3.1 input; exact external hypotheses and ℓ quantifiers remain G7.

items.name: Finite-field reduction of semisimple Frobenius
items.statement: For a rational compatible Frobenius family with a common separable rational minimal polynomial acting on stable lattices, exclude denominator/discriminant primes. The reductions are semisimple of prime-to-ℓ order; the dimension of fixed vectors equals the multiplicity of 1 in the characteristic polynomial. The common separable minimal polynomial is an input to verify, not implied by purity.

items.name: Spreading out and common semisimple Frobenius
items.statement: For Y₀ over finitely generated K₀/F_p, spread to a smooth proper family over a smooth geometrically connected finite-field base. After the permitted finite Galois extension giving connected arithmetic monodromy, choose a common closed point with semisimple Frobenius on every rational coefficient realization as supplied by Larsen–Pink. Use 108 for reduction.

api.name: commonFrobeniusModel.spread
api.statement: Expose a smooth finite-field base, the smooth proper family and its identification with the original generic fibre after the permitted extension.

api.name: commonFrobeniusModel.commonPoint
api.statement: Expose one closed point with the required semisimple Frobenius for all coefficient realizations, using the precise Larsen–Pink input in G6.

uses.how: pass from finitely generated fields to one closed-point Frobenius

items.name: Arithmetic semisimplicity from geometric subgroup and Frobenius
items.statement: For the finite residual arithmetic image, the geometric image is normal and semisimple by Theorem 1.1, and the arithmetic image is generated by it and the selected Frobenius of order prime to ℓ. Average a geometric-equivariant retraction over that cyclic subgroup to obtain arithmetic semisimplicity.

items.name: Arithmetic invariant ranks and fullness transfer
items.statement: In the spread-out setting, arithmetic invariants equal Frobenius-fixed geometric invariants. Theorem 1.3 matches geometric invariant ranks, while the common Frobenius polynomial on geometric invariants and semisimplicity match the 1-eigenspace ranks over Qℓ and Fℓ. Together with 107's cycle-image rank equality this proves 106.

items.name: Low-degree corestriction-restriction already built
items.statement: For a topological group G, open finite-index subgroup U and topological coefficient module M under the continuous-cochain hypotheses, the explicit H¹ maps satisfy cor_U^G∘res_U^G=[G:U]·id. This is credited only on Tau Ceti's explicit H¹ carrier; the comparison to canonical continuousCohomology for compact coefficients is still required.

items.name: Larsen Nori-dimension bound
items.statement: For each n there is A_n such that for prime ℓ>A_n and closed Γ⊂GL_n(Zℓ), with G the Qℓ-Zariski closure, dim N(reduction Γ)≤dimG. The full published proof was read and is decomposed through132–136; Nori and p-adic analytic growth remain recursive inputs in G1.

items.name: Larsen equality-case bounded index
items.statement: In 113, if Nori dimension equals dimG and the radical of G° is unipotent, then [G(Qℓ)∩GL_n(Zℓ):Γ]≤C_n, a constant depending only on n. Connected semisimple G satisfies the radical hypothesis. The equality-case openness and congruence-filtration comparison are prerequisites of this bound.

items.name: Building and parahoric foundations are imported
items.statement: Construct relative roots, valued root data, apartments, the building action, facets and smooth affine parahoric models with their generic fibres, special reductive quotients and congruence kernels. These existing planned foundations feed 72–80; the new extension owns only the precise hyperspecial comparison and monodromy-specific dimension argument.

api.name: parahoricFoundations.facetModel
api.statement: From the existing valued-root/building data expose the smooth affine parahoric model and its generic identification.

api.name: parahoricFoundations.reductiveQuotient
api.statement: Expose the special fibre unipotent radical and reductive quotient, with the stated congruence-kernel comparison.

items.name: Uniform weight projectors on arithmetic subquotients
items.statement: In C choose one rational-point Frobenius and its finitely many degree-w rational polynomials P_w. Their root weights are pairwise disjoint, so after excluding denominators and pairwise resultants the Chinese remainder theorem gives integral polynomials e_w(F) acting on H* exactly as its cohomological-degree projections. Every arithmetic-stable submodule or quotient is stable under F, hence under these projectors, and splits by degree. Saturation/freeness passes to each direct factor. This reduces the total-cohomology assertions in Theorem 4.5 to the single-degree proofs uniformly in the subquotient.
items.locator: Explicit extraction dévissage for §5.2–5.3 pp.218–219; based on Fact 3.2 and the CRT
items.note: Added proof detail, not a separately numbered source theorem and not an allegation of an error. The e_w(F) commute with π₀ because on H* they equal its canonical degree projectors, not because an arbitrary Frobenius is central.

items.name: Semisimple group scheme over Zℓ
items.statement: A semisimple Zℓ-group scheme is smooth affine with connected semisimple geometric fibres. It is simply connected when each geometric fibre is. The fibre root data are constant in the sense used by SGA3 XXII Proposition 2.8; this relative notion is distinct from the built field predicates.

api.name: semisimpleIntegralModel.geometricFibres
api.statement: The model is smooth affine with connected semisimple geometric fibres; fibrewise simply connectedness defines its simply connected variant.

api.name: semisimpleIntegralModel.baseChange
api.statement: Base change preserves this relative predicate and the generic/special fibre identifications.

items.name: Finite-free integral representation category
items.statement: For an affine flat Zℓ-group scheme 𝒢, Rep^f_Zℓ(𝒢) has finite-free Zℓ-modules M with a morphism of group schemes 𝒢→GL(M), and intertwining Zℓ-linear maps. Construct tensor, dual, exterior powers and generic/special restriction. Do not assume the category is abelian: arbitrary cokernels need not be free.

api.name: finiteFreeGroupRepresentation.tensorDual
api.statement: Tensor products and duals of finite-free algebraic representations retain finite freeness and the canonical group actions.

api.name: finiteFreeGroupRepresentation.baseChange
api.statement: Extension of scalars commutes with tensor, dual and exterior power on finite-free representations and maps intertwining maps to intertwining maps.

items.name: Pure and mixed lisse integral sheaves
items.statement: For a lisse Zℓ-sheaf on finite-type X₀/Z, purity of weight w means that for every closed point of X₀[1/ℓ] every root of det(T−F_x) is a |k(x)|-Weil number of weight w. Mixed means a finite filtration with pure successive quotients. Rationality means each local polynomial is in Q[T]. Keep integral lattices and their rational realizations distinct, including torsion-freeness when the determinant is formed.
items.note: Existing weight owner; no new mixed-sheaf definition at the monodromy extension.

api.name: mixedLisseSheaf.pointwisePure
api.statement: Purity tests the weight of every local Frobenius eigenvalue at every eligible closed point and every complex embedding.

api.name: mixedLisseSheaf.mixedFiltration
api.statement: A mixed object is supplied with a finite filtration whose successive quotients are pure with their specified weights.

items.name: Finite-support mixed tensor multiplicities
items.statement: For a field F, finite-dimensional V and finitely supported f:N²→N, define T^f(V)=⊕_(s,t)(V^⊗s⊗(V∨)^⊗t)^⊕f(s,t), with diagonal GL(V)-action and specified coordinate injections. This adds multiplicity bookkeeping to the existing tensor carrier, not a second tensor product.
items.locator: CT16 author TI.pdf §4.2 pp.10–11; definition preceding Lemma4.2.1.1

api.name: tensorMultiplicity.summand
api.statement: Each support index and copy has its canonical injection and projection.

api.name: tensorMultiplicity.tensorDegrees
api.statement: Tensoring two summands adds their covariant and contravariant degrees separately.

items.name: Finite-type parameter family for exponential products
items.statement: Over Z[1/(r−1)!], form tuples of r² nilpotent r×r matrices and their truncated-exponential product maps. For a fully uniform family one may use the 2r² repetitions of Larsen Proposition3, with 2r⁴ scalar parameters and the constructible locus of tuples spanning a Lie subalgebra. CT16 uses a selected r²-tuple with two repetitions; the two parameter counts must not be identified.

api.name: exponentialFamily.evaluate
api.statement: Evaluation at a nilpotent tuple and parameter tuple is the ordered product of its specified truncated exponentials.

api.name: exponentialFamily.baseChange
api.statement: All matrix equations and factorial-denominator coefficients commute with base change from Z[1/(r−1)!].

items.name: Uniform Chevalley subspaces by finite stratification
items.statement: For the finite-type exponential family of121, after excluding finitely many residue characteristics there is a single finite-support multiplicity f°_r such that every required exponential subgroup U⊂GL_r is the setwise stabilizer of a subspace W_U⊂T^(f°_r)(F^r). Equality is required as subgroup schemes after arbitrary coefficient-algebra extension.

items.name: A subspace stabilizer equals its determinant-line stabilizer
items.statement: For finite-dimensional E over F and W⊂E of dimension δ, Stab_GL(E)(W)=Stab_GL(E)(Λ^δW) as group schemes. For every F-algebra A, a point g preserves W_A exactly when its exterior action preserves the rank-one direct summand det(W)_A.
items.locator: CT16 Lemma4.2.1.1 proof p.11; Plücker step

items.name: Exponentially generated groups have no characters
items.statement: An algebraic character U→G_m of an exponentially generated group is trivial as a group-scheme morphism. In particular U acts trivially on the determinant line of every finite-dimensional U-stable subspace.
items.locator: CT16 Lemma4.2.1.1 p.11; Larsen Proposition1 p.1030

items.name: Antisymmetrization embeds determinant lines into tensor powers
items.statement: For E of dimension D and δ≤D, if δ! is invertible in F, the antisymmetrization map Λ^δE→E^⊗δ is GL(E)-equivariant and injective. The composite with the wedge quotient is multiplication by δ!. A single bound ℓ>D works for every δ≤D in CT16.

items.name: Multiplicity tensor tests reduce to separate degree bounds
items.statement: If f has finite support and d bounds both s and t on that support, the pointwise stabilizer of (T^≤d(V))^U is contained in that of (T^f(V))^U. Repeated isomorphic summands add no distinct conditions. For the tensor powers of T^(f°)(V) of orders δ≤D, take d≥D max(s,t) over supp(f°), after expanding every summand.

items.name: Pointwise tensor-stabilizer subgroup scheme
items.statement: For an algebraic representation E of GL(V) over F and a vector subspace W⊂E, Fix(W) is the closed subgroup scheme whose A-points fix every w⊗1, w∈W, in E⊗F A, for every F-algebra A. This is distinct from setwise Stab(W).

api.name: pointwiseStabilizer.points_iff
api.statement: An A-point belongs exactly when it fixes the base changes of all vectors of a chosen F-basis of W.

api.name: pointwiseStabilizer.basis_independent
api.statement: Changing the basis of W leaves its defining fixed-vector ideal unchanged.

items.name: Characteristic-zero criterion for exponential generation
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero field F, an algebraic subgroup G⊂GL_n is exponentially generated exactly when it has no nontrivial finite, toric or anisotropic quotient.

items.name: Nori correspondence for nilpotently generated Lie algebras
items.statement: For each n and all sufficiently large characteristics, Lie and exponential generation identify the relevant exponentially generated subgroups of GL_n with Lie subalgebras of gl_n spanned by nilpotent elements. For a finite residual subgroup, the dimension of the span of its order-p logarithms is the dimension of its Nori envelope.
items.locator: Larsen Proposition3 pp.1032–1033 and Theorem7 p.1035, citing Nori TheoremA

items.name: Finite set of exponential-group Hilbert polynomials
items.statement: For fixed n there are N and finitely many Hilbert polynomials for the reduced projective sets G∪(P^(n²) minus GL_n) attached to exponentially generated subgroups over fields of characteristic zero or prime not dividing N. The boundary is included; this is not just the projective closure of G.

items.name: Reduced closed fibre images in a finite-type family
items.statement: For X finite type over Z, Y⊂P^m_X closed and ξ:Z→Y finite type with every fibre image closed, after inverting one integer there is a finite-type stratified cover X′→X and Y′⊂P^m_(X′) whose fibre at an F-rational lift of x is the reduced image ξ(Z_x).

items.name: Nori dimension of a compact matrix group
items.statement: For Π⊂GL_n(F_p), Ndim(Π)=dim N(Π). For a compact subgroup Γ⊂GL_n(Z_p), define Ndim(Γ) using its reduction image. This depends on the chosen lattice representation and is distinct from the dimension of the rational Zariski closure.

api.name: noriDimension.reduction
api.statement: The compact-group value is the envelope dimension of its finite reduction image.

api.name: noriDimension.plus
api.statement: Taking the residual plus subgroup does not change the set of order-p generators or the envelope dimension.

items.name: Congruence filtration of a compact matrix group
items.statement: For closed H⊂GL_n(Z_p) and m≥1, F_mH={h∈H:h≡1 mod p^m}. The map h↦(h−1)/p^m mod p identifies F_mH/F_(m+1)H with an F_p-subspace of M_n(F_p).

api.name: congruenceFiltration.gradedMap
api.statement: The graded map sends 1+p^mA to A modulo p and has kernel the next congruence level.

api.name: congruenceFiltration.closed
api.statement: Each level is a closed normal subgroup, is open in H, and the intersection of all levels is trivial.

uses.how: Lift logarithms and reconstruct the first congruence kernel

items.name: Powers of a lifted exponential detect its logarithm
items.statement: If p≥2n, x∈M_n(F_p) is nilpotent, and A∈GL_n(Z_p) reduces to exp(x), then for every k≥1, A^(p^k)≡1+p^k M mod p^(k+1), where M is any integral lift of x.

items.name: Congruence growth bounds Nori dimension
items.statement: For large p and H=G(Q_p)∩GL_n(Z_p), the graded congruence dimensions are at most dim G. If Γ⊂H is closed, they are at least Ndim Γ on F_mΓ/F_(m+1)Γ for every m≥1. Consequently Ndim Γ≤dim G.

items.name: Equal congruence dimensions imply equal first kernels
items.statement: In135, if Ndim Γ=dim G then F_1Γ=F_1H; hence Γ is open in H and in G(Q_p). Closedness of Γ is essential.

items.name: Large-prime component-group bound
items.statement: Under the equality hypothesis of136, G/G° has prime-to-p order and a normal abelian subgroup of index bounded only by n. This concerns the finite algebraic component group represented by the compact image.

items.name: Totally ramified extension removes anisotropic quotients
items.statement: For connected G/Q_p with unipotent radical equal to its solvable radical, there is a finite totally ramified F/Q_p such that G_F has no nontrivial anisotropic quotient, while its residue field is still F_p. Then G_F is exponentially generated by128.

items.name: Uniform component bound for the flat integral closure
items.statement: For the exponential generic group G_F in138, the closure in GL_n,O_F is flat and its special fibre has at most d_n geometric irreducible components, uniformly in G and large p. Its dimension is dim G_F.

items.name: Finite-field points of connected algebraic groups
items.statement: For a smooth connected linear algebraic group K/F_p of dimension d, (p−1)^d≤|K(F_p)|≤(p+1)^d. A finite-type possibly nonreduced group has the same F_p-points as its reduction; the component estimate gives |K(F_p)|≤c(p+1)^d when it has at most c geometric components of dimension d.

items.name: Equal-kernel point counts give uniform compact index
items.statement: If Γ,H have the equal first congruence kernel of136 and the radical hypothesis of138 holds, their finite reductions satisfy |H/F_1H|≤d_n(3/2)^(n²)p^d and |Γ/F_1Γ|≥e_n⁻¹2^(−n²)p^d, with d=Ndim Γ. Thus [H:Γ]≤3^(n²)d_ne_n independently of p and Γ.

items.name: Full-dimensional closed subscheme of an integral variety
items.statement: If X is an integral finite-type scheme over a field and Z⊂X is closed with dim Z=dim X, then Z=X as schemes. This is the precise final equality step after G_s⊂Nori and equality of dimensions.

items.name: Explicit continuous H¹ and coefficient maps already built
items.statement: For a topological group G and a topological additive commutative G-module M with continuous action, TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1 is the additive quotient of continuous one-cocycles by g↦g·m−m. The carrier and explicitCoeff1 allow nondiscrete coefficients. No discrete topology is imposed on the group or coefficient module by these declarations. Its inherited pointwise topology is not identified with the canonical compact-open cohomology topology.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

api.name: H1pi_eq_zero_iff
api.statement: The class of a continuous one-cocycle is zero exactly when it lies in B1.

api.name: explicitCoeff1
api.statement: A continuous equivariant additive coefficient map induces postcomposition on classes; identity and composition laws hold.

api.name: explicitCoeff1_mk
api.statement: The image of the class of c is represented by the coefficient map composed with c.

items.name: Topological module homology uses the ordinary image
items.statement: At the pinned Mathlib, TopModuleCat.ker is the linear kernel with subspace topology and TopModuleCat.coker is the quotient by the linear range, not its closure. Its CategoryWithHomology construction therefore has the ordinary algebraic kernel/image subquotient as underlying module.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Compact-open currying already built
items.statement: For locally compact spaces X,Y and any topological Z, Homeomorph.curry identifies C(X×Y,Z) with C(X,C(Y,Z)), with compact-open topologies. Repeated currying flattens the canonical nested continuous coinduction when G is profinite.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

api.name: ContinuousMap.curry_apply
api.statement: For f:C(X×Y,Z), f.curry x y=f(x,y).

api.name: Homeomorph.curry
api.statement: If X,Y are locally compact, currying and uncurrying are inverse continuous maps for the compact-open topology.

items.name: Nonempty finite inverse systems have a section
items.statement: For a directed preorder J and F:Jᵒᵖ→Type with every F(j) finite and nonempty, F.sections is nonempty. Transition maps need not be surjective.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Scalar structure on the existing explicit H¹ quotient
items.statement: Let R be a commutative topological ring, M a topological R-module and G a topological group acting continuously by R-linear maps. The existing additive H1 carrier143 acquires an R-module structure by r[c]=[g↦r c(g)]. Every continuous R-linear equivariant coefficient map induces an R-linear map.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

items.statement: For profinite G, a commutative topological ring R and a topological R-module M with jointly continuous R-linear G-action, the underlying R-module of continuousCohomology 1 (TopRep of M) is naturally R-linearly equivalent to143 equipped with147. items.name: Continuous linear sections of finite free lattice quotients
items.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer π and fraction field K. For an exact sequence0→A→H→B→0 of finite free R-modules with their π-adic topologies, H→B has an R-linear continuous section. Its formation need not be natural or G-equivariant. Finite free Hom modules have their π-adic topology and the conjugation action of continuous lattice representations is jointly continuous.

items.name: Invariant lifting obstruction in continuous H¹
items.statement: For a complete DVR R, uniformizer π, finite free continuous G-lattice M with its π-adic topology, there is a natural exact sequence0→M^G/πM^G→(M/πM)^G→H1(G,M)[π]→0 of R-modules. On an invariant residue class m̄ choose a lift m and send it to [g↦(g·m−m)/π]. This does not require compactness of G.

items.name: Rationalization kernel is exactly lattice torsion
items.statement: For a complete DVR R with fraction field K=R[1/π], a finite free continuous G-lattice M and V=M⊗R K with its usual finite-dimensional K-topology, ker(H1(G,M)→H1(G,V)) is exactly the π-primary torsion. Thus this coefficient map is injective whenever H1(G,M)[π]=0. Compactness of G is not needed.

items.name: The extension Hom lattice is a saturated equivariant block
items.statement: For an exact sequence of finite free R-lattices0→A→H→B→0 with continuous action by an ambient group Γ, the canonical map Hom_R(B,A)→End_R(H), f↦i∘f∘p, is Γ-equivariant, injective and has finite free cokernel. In particular it is saturated. If A=H^Π for a normal subgroup Π⊲Γ, then A is Γ-stable; if B=H/A is free, this applies to the geometric invariant extension.

items.name: Continuous H¹ of a tower of finite coefficients
items.statement: Let M_n be an inverse sequence of finite discrete abelian G-modules with continuous actions and equivariant transition maps, and let M=lim_n M_n with its inverse-limit topology and action. Then the coefficient maps give an additive isomorphism H1_cont(G,M)≃lim_n H1_cont(G,M_n). No surjectivity assumption on transitions or finiteness assumption on the whole groups H1(G,M_n) is required. This is a degree-one statement, not an all-degree derived-limit comparison.

items.name: Conditional H¹ surjectivity for a lattice quotient
items.statement: Let R be a complete DVR with finite residue field of characteristic ℓ, G profinite, and0→A→H→B→0 an exact sequence of finite free continuous R-lattices. If, for every n≥1, H2_cont(G,A/π^n A)=0 and H1_cont(G,A/π^n A) is finite, then H1_cont(G,H)→H1_cont(G,B) is surjective. Finite-level cohomology uses discrete coefficients; the conclusion uses lattice coefficients. The vanishing hypothesis is on Tau Ceti’s explicit discrete H2 carrier. A geometric cd assertion on another model must first be transported through the upstream discrete comparison; that interface is part of the remaining geometric application gap.
items.locator: CHT §1.3 p.208, §5.2 pp.218–219 and §10 pp.230–232; direct coefficient proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Discrete coefficient H¹ exactness already built
items.statement: For a discrete short exact sequence of continuous G-modules0→A→B→C→0, the range of H1(A)→H1(B) equals the kernel of H1(B)→H1(C), and the range of H1(B)→H1(C) equals the kernel of the explicit connecting map to H2(A). Here G is a topological group, all three coefficients are discrete, and H1/H2 are Tau Ceti explicit continuous carriers.
